sentence: This project builds computer tools that analyze single cell and spatial genomics datasets to help find pathways driving immunosuppression in glioblastoma.
This project maintains a database of information about the laboratory mouse to help scientists study the genetic and genomic basis of human biology and disease.
This project tests whether long-term alcohol drinking harms a brain region called the nucleus reuniens, hurting working memory and attention.
This project tests how long a gene editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy keeps working in a humanized mouse model.
This project works on ways to manage, prevent and reverse type 1 diabetes using biomedical engineering.
This project shares high-throughput methods for mapping neuronal projections so labs can study how brain circuitry is disrupted in animal models of autism and schizophrenia.
This project studies how DNA damage switches the forms of a regulator of a tumor suppressor gene, and how this connects to cancer.
This project studies how lipid oxidation in the retina produces molecules that promote inflammation and contribute to age-related macular degeneration.
This project studies how cells behave on porous membranes and designs membranes for lab models of tissue barriers and cell communication.
This project tries to find out how parts of the immune system work together to make antibodies that protect against HIV.
This project studies how undernutrition lowers luteinizing hormone release, looking at a neuron-based signal and an immune-based signal in the brain.
This project studies how RNA interference helps silence genes and keep chromosomes stable in yeast and mammalian cells.
This project studies how bone marrow niche cells affect platelet activation and red blood cell production in sickle cell disease.
This project looks for genes that change how insects and humans respond to combinations of insecticides.
This project profiles the genetic, metabolic, immune, spatial and functional properties of cells in pancreas tissue from organ donors with type 1 diabetes.
This project studies how hardship during life affects stress regulation, aging and mental health in midlife adults followed for many years.
This project provides a mass spectrometer that measures the mass and structure of biomolecules such as proteins and peptides.
This project studies how the three-dimensional folding of DNA and histone modifications affect RNA splicing.
This project collects and analyzes MRI and amyloid and tau imaging of the brain to help diagnose neurodegenerative diseases.
This project tests whether toluene narrows cerebral arteries by acting on a type of ion channel in artery muscle.
